story_title: Crop Yield Trends and Performance Across Varieties and Sites (1931-1932)
story_subtitle: Analyzing yield variations, site performance, and annual comparisons for different crop varieties

story_pieces.narration: In 1931, the highest individual yields were recorded for Trebi in Waseca (63.83) and Wisconsin No. 38 in Waseca (58.8). These varieties demonstrated exceptional performance across multiple sites.
story_pieces.question: Which varieties and sites achieved the highest yields in 1931?
story_pieces.visualization: ranked bar chart (variety and site vs. yield)

story_pieces.narration: The Morris site had the highest average yield for several varieties in 1931, including Trebi (43.77) and No. 462 (44.7), while Grand Rapids consistently had the lowest yields for most varieties.
story_pieces.question: Which site had the highest average yield for different varieties in 1931?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (site vs. average yield per variety)

story_pieces.narration: Trebi and Wisconsin No. 38 consistently outperformed other varieties, with Trebi showing the highest average yield in 1931 (45.26) and Wisconsin No. 38 in 1932 (35.95).
story_pieces.question: Which varieties had the highest average yields across all sites and years?

story_pieces.narration: From 1931 to 1932, most varieties experienced yield declines, with Manchuria dropping from 34.96 to 26.94 and Svansota from 31.19 to 25.46. However, Wisconsin No. 38 showed a slight increase in 1932.
story_pieces.question: How did crop yields change between 1931 and 1932 for each variety?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (year vs. average yield per variety)

story_pieces.narration: Yield variability across sites was most pronounced for No. 475, with yields ranging from 19.70 (Grand Rapids) to 46.77 (Waseca). In contrast, Velvet showed relatively consistent performance across sites.
story_pieces.question: Which sites showed the most variability in yields across different crop varieties?
